body:
# Independent audit of stationary section tails and the optimized disk profile

Audited `candidate 87728f667e65240d` in full. Result:
PASS after the zero-fiber integral correction described below. The
statement retains one integer variable and d>=2; it does not claim OC.

## Required measure correction, now applied

The initial version set s_z=0 outside I_+ but left the distinct section
integrals in (3) and (5) summed over all z. Since Q_z remained the actual
section, a former zero-d-volume fiber could contribute positive
H_(d-1) mass to those integrals. Setting a separate scalar s_z to zero
does not suppress that contribution. The disk-plus-segment example in
`candidate 867dbbe22c30cda2` witnesses the error.

The author corrected both formulas to sum their section integrals
explicitly over z in I_+. This now agrees with the derivative measure,
the centroid identities, and the later zero-fiber discussion.

## Section theorem and sharpness

For a nonzero continuous normal u, graph differentiation in its unit
direction supplies exactly the factor 1/|u| in the fiber cap derivative.
The integer component a does not change this within-fiber Jacobian.
Condition (2) removes all graph points lying at an interval endpoint,
up to zero projected (d-1)-measure, and compactness bounds the difference
quotients. Thus the first variation is valid for every stated regular
cap, without a smoothness assumption on the bodies.

Full-normal stationarity gives the full first moments displayed in
(3). If one instead fixes |u|, the tangent-normal argument and the
integrated plane equation give the same result. The central section
has positive (d-1)-measure because its point is interior to K_m.

The parametrization (6) is an isometry on each integer fiber. Its
different ambient plane Jacobian is correctly excluded from the mixed
measure. The relative section is a genuine d-dimensional convex body:
the original plane has ambient interior points of C on both sides.
Brunn-Minkowski therefore gives concave (d-1)-st roots for its positive
section-fiber volumes.

For n=1, both the positive original d-volume indices and the positive
section-volume indices are integer intervals. Their intersection is
an interval as well, so removing the former zero-d-volume fibers only
truncates endpoints of the positive section sequence. It cannot remove
an internal positive node. This is the exact fact needed to preserve
the concave-root hypothesis after deletion; the note does not assume
an analogous truncation assertion for multiple integer variables.

The surviving mean is the integer m. Applying the scalar theorem with
root degree d-1 produces gamma_d exactly. If only one positive section
fiber survives, the scalar singleton case applies. Both closed integer
sides retain the full central section mass. The d=1/H_0 branch is
explicitly outside the theorem and the sweep section; no zero root
degree or inappropriate counting-measure substitution occurs.

For sharpness, the author's clarification that T has ordinary centroid
zero makes every continuous moment explicit. The cone-product C is
full-dimensional, each positive original fiber has a regular t=0
section, and the integer section masses are exactly the scalar
sharpness sequence. The shear preserves the lattice and each fiber's
measure. This proves sharpness under stationarity; the note correctly
does not assert a minimizing normal for that family.

## Sweep identities

The individual thresholds are b-a(b)(z-m). Their derivatives give

    V'=-S,
    V_-'=-S_- -a'T,
    V_+'=-S_+ +a'T.

The opposite torque signs are correct. The two closed sides double-count
the central fiber, consistently in both volume and derivative formulas.
Integer-tilt stationarity suffices for the section-tail bounds; no
continuous-centroid identity is silently required in this part.

The correction integrals cancel precisely the two torque terms. Their
differences are integrals of S_- and S_+, respectively, and hence lie
between gamma_d times the total swept volume and the whole swept volume.
No uncorrected claim is made when a varies. Extending a fixed-tilt
identity to an empty cap requires the stated hypotheses along that
whole path; existence of such a path is not asserted.

The initial draft included an explicit extra continuity hypothesis for
ordinary derivatives. In fact, with fixed unit e this can be verified
directly: each fiber cap is the integral of a bounded section function
f_z over a ray. The function f_z is continuous at every regular level
(interior continuity follows from Brunn-Minkowski; a regular supporting
level has zero section area and the same limiting area). Composition
with the C^1 threshold gives the derivative, while bounded section
areas give absolute continuity. This supplies the needed regularity
without any uniform smoothness of the bodies.

## Globally minimizing optimized disk profile

For the two unit endpoint disks the cap sum is even in the integer
tilt v. At a nonnegative scalar threshold t its derivative for v>=0
is f_1(t-v)-f_1(t+v)>=0, using evenness and radial decrease of the
chord-length function. Thus zero tilt is a global optimizer. At a
negative threshold, the endpoint sum is at least pi, and the central
radius-two cap is at least 2pi.

At y_t=(0,0,t), 0<t<1, every unit continuous normal has scalar threshold
s in [-t,t]. Nonnegative s give optimized cap volume at least V(t);
negative s give at least 3pi>V(t). Pure integer normals give at least
5pi. This covers every ambient orientation and proves that the stated
horizontal cap is an actual global minimizing containing cap. Moving
a containing boundary to y_t only decreases its mass, so there is no
omitted class of containing halfspaces. Nonvertical boundaries have
zero disk area; vertical boundaries retain complete fibers as counted.

Every section in this path is proper, regular, and has centroid y_t.
The exact derivatives are

    V'=-2sqrt(4-t^2)-4sqrt(1-t^2),
    V''=2t/sqrt(4-t^2)+4t/sqrt(1-t^2).

As t increases to one, V tends to the positive disk-cap area
4pi/3-sqrt(3), V' has a finite limit, and V'' tends to positive infinity.
Consequently V V''+(p-1)(V')^2 is positive near that endpoint for every
fixed p>0. This rigorously refutes every positive-power concavity claim
for the optimized profile, even along the asserted global minimizing
stationary path. The body still has a depth-one-half symmetry center;
the example is not an OC counterexample.

## Added square-product obstruction

The later Section 4 was audited separately and also passes. For
0<b<1 and |a|<1-b, every section height b+a,b,b-a lies strictly
inside its square. Each section has length two and full section
centroid (0,0,b). The centrally symmetric mixed subset with vertical
interval [2b-1,1] has exactly 12(1-b) area; hence its half-mass argument
proves the claimed global minimum 6(1-b) against every ambient cap.

At b=1/2,a=-9/20 the individual cap areas are 19/10,1,1/10. The
right-integer part therefore occupies 11/30 of this actual minimizing
cap, strictly below gamma_2=4/9 by 7/90. This is fully compatible with
the section-side fraction four sixths; those are different measures.

For the second path, a(b)=4(b-9/20) on [2/5,1/2] remains within
the strict proper-section range. Direct differentiation of the three
rectangle areas gives exactly V'=-6,V_+'=4,V_-'=-12. The same values
follow from S=6,S_-=S_+=4,T=2 and a'=4. Thus the uncorrected right-side
swept-volume inequality fails at regular globally minimizing caps, not
merely at singular endpoint levels. The points are not asserted to be
globally deepest points of S.
